meta.description: Multi-source literature search, citation verification, strict independent other-citation audits, article-level citation metric tables, influential citer profiling with citation-context extraction, MeSH search strategy, citation file management (.nbib/.ris/.bib conversion), and reference management (BibTeX, related articles, ID conversion) via MCP tools (PubMed, CrossRef, arXiv, Scopus, ScienceDirect). Use for coordinated literature workflows beyond one MCP call.

scientific_integrity.detail: Uses validated academic APIs (PubMed, CrossRef, arXiv, Scopus) with proper citations. No data fabrication.

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for literature search and citation management. Does not overstep into clinical decision-making.

methodological_ground.detail: Follows standard bibliometric practices. T1→T2→T3 source routing is well-established. MeSH strategy aligns with NLM guidelines.

code_usability.detail: Includes working fallback scripts (academic_search.py, format-converter.py). MCP server startup commands provided.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of literature workflows: multi-source search, citation verification, MeSH strategy, file conversion, reference management, and strict other-citation audits. All major use cases addressed.

reliability.note: Robust T1→T2→T3 fallback chain. Error handling for MCP tool failures and no-results scenarios. Stdlib-only fallback when MCP unavailable. Minor: lacks retry logic specification.

performance_context.note: Efficient routing protocol loads only needed workflows. Static/dynamic split keeps context lean. Pre-flight check script prevents wasted batch operations.

agent_usability.note: Excellent router design with clear 5-step protocol. Manifest-driven workflow detection. Self-documenting via always_load and on_demand references. Agent reads only what it needs.

human_usability.note: Well-structured documentation. Manifest.yaml provides clear overview. Setup instructions for API keys and proxy. Minor: multilingual triggers (Chinese keywords) may confuse non-Chinese users.

security.note: API keys via environment variables, not hardcoded. Uses pybliometrics config for Elsevier keys. Polite API usage with mailto headers. No credential leakage risk.

maintainability.note: Excellent modular architecture. Static layer versioned and reviewable. Shared modules prevent duplication. Adding new workflows only requires updating manifest and creating workflow file.

agent_specific.note: Strong routing logic and lazy loading. Clear separation of concerns. Workflow files link to shared modules. Minor: no explicit token budget management for large citation audits. Missing workflow execution examples.

key_strengths: Excellent modular architecture with static/dynamic split enabling efficient context usage and maintainable workflow expansion
Comprehensive coverage of academic literature workflows from search to citation audit, with bilingual support (English/Chinese)
Robust fallback mechanisms: T1→T2→T3 source routing, MCP-to-stdlib degradation, zero-results handling
Strong security practices: environment-based API key management, polite API usage with rate limiting awareness
Agent-friendly design: manifest-driven workflow detection, lazy loading of references, clear 5-step routing protocol

recommendations.title: Add token budget management for large citation audits
recommendations.problem: Strict other-citation audits (wf6) with hundreds of citing papers could exceed context limits or API quotas without incremental processing guidance.
recommendations.root_cause: No explicit pagination or batching strategy in workflow files for high-volume operations.
recommendations.fix: Add batch-size parameters to wf6 (e.g., process 50 citers at a time, checkpoint progress). Document token estimation heuristics (e.g., ~500 tokens per citer profile).

recommendations.title: Enhance citation verification mismatch diagnostics
recommendations.problem: When citations don't match MCP records, error reporting is generic ("citation not found") rather than identifying specific field mismatches (title, authors, year, DOI).
recommendations.root_cause: citation-parser.md module lacks field-level comparison logic.
recommendations.fix: Extend parser to return structured diff (which fields differ, by how much). Add fuzzy matching for author names and title variations.

recommendations.title: Add workflow execution examples to SKILL.md
recommendations.problem: Router protocol is clear, but first-time users lack concrete examples showing how user queries map to workflow file loading and execution.
recommendations.root_cause: Documentation focuses on structure but lacks end-to-end traces.
recommendations.fix: Add 2-3 worked examples in SKILL.md showing: (1) user query → detected workflow → files loaded → execution steps, (2) combined workflow scenario, (3) fallback scenario.
